title: Domestic Workers Convention, 2011 (No. 189)
sum: The first treaty on domestic work: decent work, equal treatment on hours, rest, minimum wage and social security, written terms for migrant workers before departure, and regulation of agencies.

title: Domestic Workers Recommendation, 2011 (No. 201)
sum: Guidance on implementing C189: hours records, on-call time, accommodation standards, model contracts, repatriation and cooperation between states.

title: Private Employment Agencies Convention, 1997 (No. 181)
sum: Agencies may not charge workers fees; states must protect migrant workers recruited by agencies and investigate complaints.

title: Migration for Employment Convention (Revised), 1949 (No. 97)
sum: Equal treatment of regular migrant workers with nationals on pay, hours, union rights, accommodation and social security.

title: Migrant Workers (Supplementary Provisions) Convention, 1975 (No. 143)
sum: Basic rights of all migrant workers, measures against clandestine movements, and free choice of employment after a period.

title: Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190)
sum: Right to a world of work free from violence and harassment, expressly including private households as workplaces.

title: Protocol of 2014 to the Forced Labour Convention, 1930
sum: Prevention of forced labor, protection of victims and access to remedies, including protection from abusive recruitment.

title: Freedom of Association and Protection of the Right to Organise Convention, 1948 (No. 87)
sum: Workers without distinction may form and join organizations of their choosing.

title: Worst Forms of Child Labour Convention, 1999 (No. 182)
sum: Hazardous child domestic work may be listed as a worst form of child labor.

title: General Principles and Operational Guidelines for Fair Recruitment, and Definition of Recruitment Fees and Related Costs
sum: No recruitment fees or related costs should be charged to workers; the 2018 definition lists the costs covered.

title: ILO Multilateral Framework on Labour Migration
sum: Non-binding principles on labor migration governance, including domestic workers as a group at risk.

title: International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families
sum: Rights of all migrant workers regardless of status, including equal treatment in conditions of work, protection of identity documents (art. 21) and duties of states of origin.

title: Committee on Migrant Workers, General Comment No. 1 on migrant domestic workers
sum: Applies the convention to domestic work: written contracts, mobility between employers, access to justice, privacy, and pre-departure duties of states of origin.

title: Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
sum: Equality in employment and protection from discrimination, the basis for scrutiny of sex-specific migration bans.

title: CEDAW General Recommendation No. 26 on women migrant workers
sum: States should lift sex-specific bans on migration, regulate domestic work, and protect women at every stage of migration.

title: CEDAW General Recommendation No. 38 on trafficking in women and girls in the context of global migration
sum: Addresses demand for exploitative domestic labor and the role of sponsorship systems in trafficking.

title: International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
sum: Right to just and favourable conditions of work (art. 7) and to social security (art. 9).

title: CESCR General Comment No. 23 on the right to just and favourable conditions of work
sum: Domestic workers must enjoy equal hours, rest and leave; migrant domestic workers are named as a group needing protection.

title: Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, Especially Women and Children
sum: Defines trafficking, including recruitment by deception or abuse of vulnerability for forced labor or servitude.

title: Report of the Special Rapporteur on contemporary forms of slavery: domestic servitude (A/HRC/15/20)
sum: Thematic report on domestic servitude, the legal exclusion of domestic workers and the role of tied visas.

title: Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration
sum: Objective 6 on fair and ethical recruitment and decent work, with a commitment to protect domestic workers.

title: ASEAN Declaration on the Protection and Promotion of the Rights of Migrant Workers (Cebu)
sum: Obligations of receiving and sending states, including fair treatment and access to justice.

title: ASEAN Consensus on the Protection and Promotion of the Rights of Migrant Workers
sum: Rights to keep identity documents, fair pay, and to file complaints; regulation of recruitment fees.

title: Colombo Process (Regional Consultative Process on Overseas Employment and Contractual Labour for Countries of Origin in Asia)
sum: Dialogue among Asian countries of origin on recruitment, skills and welfare.

title: Abu Dhabi Dialogue among Asian countries of origin and destination
sum: Interregional dialogue; work streams on recruitment, contracts and domestic workers.

title: Arab Charter on Human Rights
sum: Prohibits forced labor and trafficking (art. 10) and protects the right to work (art. 34).

title: African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights
sum: Right to work under equitable and satisfactory conditions (art. 15).

title: Protocol on the Rights of Women in Africa (Maputo Protocol)
sum: Equal pay and protection of women in informal work, including domestic work (art. 13).

title: Protocol to the Treaty Establishing the African Economic Community relating to Free Movement of Persons
sum: Right of establishment and residence for workers across member states (not yet in force).

title: SADC Labour Migration Policy Framework
sum: Regional policy on protecting migrant workers, including domestic workers.

title: European Convention on Human Rights, art. 4 (as read in Siliadin v France, 2005, and C.N. v United Kingdom, 2012)
sum: States must criminalize servitude and forced labor; both leading cases concerned migrant domestic workers.

title: European Social Charter (Revised), art. 19
sum: Equal treatment of migrant workers lawfully within the territory in pay, conditions and union membership.

title: Council of Europe Convention on Action against Trafficking in Human Beings
sum: Victim identification, recovery period and residence permits for trafficked persons, including domestic workers.

title: Council of Europe Convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence (Istanbul Convention)
sum: Protection from violence against women, with autonomous residence status for migrant victims (art. 59).

title: Council Directive 89/391/EEC on safety and health at work
sum: The framework directive excludes domestic servants from its scope (art. 3(a)).

title: Directive 2009/52/EC on sanctions against employers of illegally staying third-country nationals
sum: Back pay and complaint mechanisms for irregular workers, including those in private households.

title: Directive (EU) 2024/1233 on a single application procedure for a single permit (recast)
sum: Holders of a single permit may change employer, subject to notification.

title: American Convention on Human Rights
sum: Prohibits slavery, servitude and forced labor (art. 6).

title: Additional Protocol in the Area of Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (Protocol of San Salvador)
sum: Just and equitable conditions of work, rest and paid holidays (art. 7).

title: Inter-American Convention on the Prevention, Punishment and Eradication of Violence against Women (Belém do Pará)
sum: Covers violence in the home and the workplace, including against domestic workers.

title: Advisory Opinion OC-18/03, Juridical Condition and Rights of Undocumented Migrants
sum: Labor rights arise from the employment relationship whatever the worker's migration status.

title: MERCOSUR Residence Agreement
sum: Nationals of member states may reside and work in another member state.

title: MoU on the Recruitment and Placement of Indonesian Domestic Workers in Malaysia
sum: One-channel recruitment system, wage, rest day and document rules.

title: Agreement on the Placement and Protection of Indonesian Domestic Workers
sum: Standard contract, wage payment through banks and access to communication.

title: Agreement on Labour Cooperation for Domestic Service Workers Recruitment
sum: Standard contract, wage, rest and the worker's right to keep their passport.

title: Agreement on the Employment of Domestic Workers
sum: Worker keeps passport and phone, eight hours' rest, no transfer without consent of the worker.

title: Memorandum of Understanding on Domestic Workers
sum: Standard contract and joint committee.

title: Labour Cooperation Agreement for Domestic Service Workers Recruitment
sum: Standard contract and wage payment through banks.

title: Agreement on Domestic Service Workers Recruitment
sum: Standard contract and dispute settlement.

title: Agreement on the Recruitment of Domestic Workers
sum: Recruitment costs borne by the employer and a standard contract.

title: Agreement on the Recruitment of Domestic Workers
sum: Standard contract and protection duties.

title: Bilateral Labour Agreement on Domestic Workers
sum: Resumption of recruitment under a standard contract.

title: Agreement on the Recruitment of Domestic Workers
sum: Standard contract and protection duties.

title: Bilateral Agreement on the Recruitment of Domestic Workers
sum: Standard contract.

title: Memorandum of Understanding on Domestic Workers
sum: Employer pays recruitment costs; standard contract.

title: Federal Decree-Law No. 9 of 2022 on Domestic Workers
sum: Recruitment licensing, employment agreement, rest, leave, wage payment, transfer, inspection, disputes and penalties for domestic workers. Replaced Federal Law No. 10 of 2017.

title: Cabinet Resolution No. 106 of 2022, Executive Regulations of the Domestic Workers Decree-Law
sum: Occupations covered, rest periods, weekly day off, and administrative penalties.

title: Ministerial Resolution No. 674 of 2022 on the transfer of domestic workers
sum: Transfer with the employer's written consent and Ministry approval, or after a judicial decision of breach.

title: Federal Decree-Law No. 21 of 2023 amending Federal Decree-Law No. 9 of 2022
sum: Ministry decides disputes up to AED 50,000, with court review within set time limits.

title: Regulation of Domestic Workers and Similar Categories (Council of Ministers Decision 310/1434)
sum: Contract, rest, leave, end-of-service award and dispute settlement; amended in 2024 (not verified).

title: Rules for Practising Recruitment and Providing Labour Services (Ministerial Decision 119698)
sum: Licensing of recruitment companies with bank guarantees; ban on taking any sum from the worker; liability for placed workers and their return costs.

title: Ministerial Decision No. 40676/1445 on domestic workers (replacing Decision 310/1434 from 21 September 2024)
sum: New framework for domestic workers, including health insurance and work-injury cover through insurance (text not yet coded).

title: Law No. 68 of 2015 on Domestic Workers
sum: Hours, rest, leave, passport rule, recruitment offices and dispute settlement.

title: Ministerial Decision No. 22 of 2022 on domestic workers
sum: Minimum wage, annual leave, overtime, phone access, document retention with consent and complaint procedure.

title: Ministerial Decision No. 574 of 2025 issuing the regulation on domestic workers and similar categories
sum: Replaces the 2004 regulation: written Arabic contract, 12-hour day with 8 hours' rest, weekly paid rest, 21 days' leave, 30 days' sick leave, end-of-service pay, ban on taking fees from workers, inspection and fee-free disputes.

title: Ministerial Regulation No. 189 of 2004 on Labour Rules and Conditions for Domestic Employees
sum: Contract, monthly pay, weekly rest, leave every two years, change of employer and complaints; no penalties.

title: Law No. 15 of 2017 on Domestic Workers
sum: Contract, maximum daily hours, weekly rest, leave and end-of-service pay.

title: Law No. 17 of 2020 on the Minimum Wage
sum: Non-discriminatory minimum wage covering domestic workers.

title: Labour Law for the Private Sector (Law No. 36 of 2012), art. 2
sum: Lists the articles that apply to domestic workers.

title: Ministerial Decision No. 574/2025 on Domestic Workers and Similar Categories
sum: Regulation of domestic work under the 2023 Labour Law.

title: Regulation No. 90 of 2009 on Domestic Workers, Cooks, Gardeners and Similar Categories
sum: Hours, weekly rest, leave and payment under the Labour Law.

title: Unified Standard Contract for Migrant Domestic Workers
sum: Contract terms required for the work permit; a 2020 revision was suspended.

title: Foreign Workers Law, 1991
sum: Written contract, housing, health insurance and passport protection for foreign workers, including caregivers.

title: Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57) and the Standard Employment Contract for Foreign Domestic Helpers (ID 407)
sum: Rest day, leave, wage protection and maternity protection; live-in rule and minimum allowable wage by policy.

title: Employment of Foreign Manpower Act and Work Pass Regulations
sum: Work permit conditions on rest, accommodation, salary payment and insurance.

title: Employment Act 1955, First Schedule (as amended 2022)
sum: Domestic employees covered by selected provisions only.

title: Employment Service Act
sum: Permits, agency rules and the ban on keeping workers' documents.

title: National Collective Agreement on Domestic Work (CCNL Lavoro Domestico)
sum: Binding pay scales, hours, rest and leave for domestic workers.

title: Royal Decree 1620/2011 on the special employment relationship of domestic service
sum: Contract, minimum wage, hours, rest and leave.

title: Royal Decree-Law 16/2022 on working and social security conditions of domestic workers
sum: Unemployment protection and an end to dismissal without cause.

title: Immigration Rules, Appendix Overseas Domestic Worker
sum: Six-month visa; change of employer allowed since 2016; no extension.

title: Fair Labor Standards Amendments of 1974 (domestic service)
sum: Minimum wage and overtime for domestic workers; live-in workers exempt from overtime.

title: William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008, s. 203
sum: Contract and protection rules for domestic workers of diplomats (A-3, G-5 visas).

title: Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, ss. 209.2-209.3 (employer conditions)
sum: Employers must not charge recruitment fees and must provide working conditions as offered.

title: Law 26.844 on the Special Employment Regime for Private Household Personnel
sum: Hours, rest, leave, minimum pay, social security and a dedicated labor tribunal.

title: Sectoral Determination 7: Domestic Worker Sector
sum: Hours, rest, leave, written particulars and pay.

title: Mahlangu v Minister of Labour (Constitutional Court)
sum: Exclusion of domestic workers from work-injury compensation held unconstitutional.

title: Law No. 18 of 2017 on the Protection of Indonesian Migrant Workers
sum: Zero-cost placement, pre-departure orientation, social security and protection abroad.

title: Minister of Manpower Decision No. 260 of 2015
sum: Suspends placement of domestic workers with individual employers in Middle East countries.

title: Republic Act No. 10361, Domestic Workers Act (Batas Kasambahay)
sum: Rights of domestic workers in the Philippines: minimum wage, rest, leave and social security.

title: Republic Act No. 11641 creating the Department of Migrant Workers
sum: Contract verification, Migrant Workers Offices abroad and welfare services.

title: Law No. 69/2020/QH14 on Vietnamese Workers Working Abroad under Contracts
sum: Contract registration, fee caps, orientation and support fund.

title: Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment Act No. 21 of 1985 (as amended)
sum: Registration, contract approval, training and insurance for migrant workers.

title: Foreign Employment Act, 2007
sum: Labor permits, welfare fund and orientation.

title: Emigration Act, 1983
sum: Emigration clearance, recruiting agent registration and protection of emigrants.

title: Overseas Employment and Migrants Act, 2013
sum: Recruitment regulation, migrants' rights and welfare.

title: Ethiopia's Overseas Employment Proclamation No. 923/2016 (amended by 1246/2021)
sum: Bilateral-agreement requirement, competency certificate and employer-paid costs.

title: Labour Institutions (Private Employment Agencies) Regulations, 2016
sum: Agency registration and fee limits.

title: Employment (Recruitment of Ugandan Migrant Workers Abroad) Regulations, 2021
sum: Agency licensing, contracts and orientation.

title: Law No. 19-12 on working and employment conditions of domestic workers
sum: Written contract, minimum age 18, weekly rest, leave, a minimum wage and labor inspector conciliation.

title: Ministerial Regulation No. 14 (B.E. 2555) on the protection of domestic workers
sum: Weekly holiday, annual and sick leave and wage payment; no minimum wage or hours limit.

title: Royal Ordinance on the Management of Foreign Workers' Employment, B.E. 2560
sum: Recruitment licensing, document retention ban and change of employer for foreign workers.

title: Punjab Domestic Workers Act, 2019
sum: Hours, weekly rest, leave, minimum wage, social security and dispute committees; bans domestic work under 15.

title: Islamabad Capital Territory Domestic Workers Act, 2022
sum: Similar protections for the federal capital territory.

title: Complementary Law No. 150 of 2015 on domestic employment
sum: Equal labor rights: hours, overtime, FGTS, unemployment insurance and social security.

title: Federal Labor Law, reform of the chapter on domestic workers (2019)
sum: Written contract, 8-hour day, weekly rest and mandatory social security.

title: Law No. 8726 reforming the Labor Code chapter on domestic work
sum: Hours, weekly rest, leave and social security.

title: Law No. 2450 regulating salaried household work
sum: Minimum wage, hours, rest and leave for household workers.

title: Law No. 31047 on household workers
sum: Written registered contract, minimum wage, 8-hour day, protection from harassment and social security.

title: Law No. 20.786 on household workers' hours, rest and pay
sum: Hours, rest days, registration of contracts and a ban on in-kind deductions.

title: Law No. 5407 on domestic work
sum: Hours, rest, leave and social security; full minimum wage from 2019 (Law 6338).

title: Law No. 18.065 on domestic work
sum: Hours, weekly rest, night rest, wage councils and home inspection with a court order.

title: Wage Order for domestic workers under the Labour Act 2007
sum: Sectoral minimum wage and conditions for domestic workers.

title: Minimum Wages and Conditions of Employment (Domestic Workers) Order, 2011
sum: Minimum wage, hours, rest and leave for domestic workers.

title: Employment and Labour Relations Act, 2004, with sectoral wage orders for domestic workers
sum: General labor rights apply to domestic workers; sectoral minimum wages.
